title: Quasi-compact quasi-separated derived base change from the single-complex condition
statement: In a cartesian square of schemes X' \xrightarrow{g'} X and S' \xrightarrow{g} S, with f:X\to S quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-base-change], write f':X'\to S' for the base change of f. Let K \in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) and let L(g')^*K \to K' be a map in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X'}) [def-pc-derived-category]. For x'\in X', put x=g'(x'), s'=f'(x') and s=f(x)=g(s'). Assume that for every x' and i\in\mathbf Z the canonical map H^i(K_x\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\mathcal O_{S',s'})\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\mathcal O_{S',s'}}\mathcal O_{X',x'}\to H^i(K'_{x'}) is an isomorphism [def-pc-single-complex-base-change-stalk-condition]. Then the composite Lg^*Rf_*K \to Rf'_*L(g')^*K \to Rf'_*K' is an isomorphism in D(\mathcal O_{S'}) [def-pc-derived-base-change-map].

proof.text: Apply the target-locality reduction with an affine-base criterion still to prove. This uses exact open restriction and compatibility of the canonical map, and introduces no global compactness assumption on S.

For the resulting square with affine bases, infer CompactSpace X from QuasiCompact f and QuasiSeparatedSpace X from QuasiSeparated f. Define P(U) to be IsIso of the explicit canonical source-open comparison. Its affine base case is the source-open affine comparison theorem.

For quasi-compact U and affine V, V is compact and U intersection V is compact by Mathlib QuasiSeparatedSpace.inter_isCompact. The source-open union theorem then combines P(U), P(V), P(U intersection V) into P(U union V). Apply quasiCompactOpen_induction to obtain P(top).
Normalize the top-open comparison to the original global comparison. This completes the affine-base criterion supplied to the target-locality reduction.
